Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the incredible journey you've been on, becoming a new mother, and I'm honored to be a part of your care team. As we navigate this postpartum period together, I want to ensure that we prioritize your emotional well-being. To help us do that, I'll be using the EPDS, which is a tool designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms. This assessment will give us a better understanding of how you're feeling and help us identify any areas where you might need extra support.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and conducted in a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and provide guidance, not to judge. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and natural as possible.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that it's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions during the postpartum period. It's okay to not feel okay, and it's okay to ask for help. We'll work through this together, and I'm committed to supporting you every step of the way.

Let's get started, shall we? The first question is: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(sighing slightly) Honestly, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty upbeat person, but since having the baby, everything just feels so... overwhelming. I do still enjoy some things, like watching my baby sleep or seeing them smile, but it's not the same as it was before. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor, you know? I'll see something that would normally make me laugh, but now it just doesn't seem as funny. I've had a few moments where I've laughed with my partner or family, but it's not as often as it used to be. And even when I do laugh, it feels kind of... forced, I guess. Like I'm trying to be happy, but it's not really genuine. (pausing, looking down) I don't know, maybe I'm just tired all the time and that's why everything feels so different. (looking up, slightly tearfully) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No, not really. Like I said, it's been hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and laughing doesn't come as easily as it used to. I've had a few moments where I've laughed, but it's not like it was before. It's like I'm trying to be happy, but it's just not feeling as natural as it used to. (sighing) I don't know, maybe I'm just too tired and stressed out all the time. (looking down, fidgeting with hands)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head slightly) Not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll plan things or think about doing something I used to enjoy, but when it comes down to it, I just don't feel like doing it. Like, my friends wanted to come over and visit the baby, and I thought that sounded nice, but when they actually came, I just felt anxious and overwhelmed. I didn't really enjoy their visit like I thought I would. And things that used to bring me joy, like reading or taking a walk, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. (pausing, looking down) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, but I'm not really enjoying anything. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but everything just feels kind of... dull, I guess. (looking up, slightly tearfully)
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always worrying that I'm doing something wrong with the baby, or that I'm not being a good enough mother. If the baby cries, I immediately think it's because I'm not doing something right, or that I'm not responding to their needs quickly enough. And even when my partner or family members try to reassure me that everything is okay, I still can't shake the feeling that I'm to blame somehow. (sighing) It's like, I know intellectually that I'm doing my best, but emotionally, I just feel like I'm failing all the time. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) And it's not just with the baby, either. If I make a mistake with something else, like cooking dinner or cleaning the house, I'll beat myself up over it, too. (pausing, looking up) I guess I just feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that's a really hard feeling to live with. (tearfully) Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a mother, and that someone is going to figure out that I have no idea what I'm doing.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about the baby's safety, like, constantly. I'll be sitting there, feeding them or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll think, "What if I'm not doing this right? What if I'm hurting them somehow?" Or I'll worry about things that might happen to them, like, "What if they roll off the bed?" or "What if they get sick?" Even when my partner or family members are taking care of the baby, I'll still worry that something is going to go wrong. (biting lip) And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about things like, "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" or "What if the baby is not gaining enough weight?" (shaking head) It's like, my mind is always racing with these worst-case scenarios, and I have trouble shutting them off. (sighing) Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just feel this wave of anxiety wash over me, and I'll think, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just relax?" (looking up, tearfully) It's exhausting, you know?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes... that's happened to me too. Sometimes I'll just be sitting there, feeding the baby or doing something routine, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to... I don't know, like I'm going to lose control or something. (shaking head) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to something, even though there's no real reason to be scared. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes it's triggered by something, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. (sighing) And when it happens, I feel so overwhelmed and helpless. I'll try to breathe deeply and calm myself down, but it's hard to shake off the feeling of fear. (looking up, tearfully) It's like, I know I'm safe, and the baby is safe, but my body is just... reacting to something, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's really scary, because I feel like I'm not in control of my own emotions.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a lump form in throat) Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it all just feels so overwhelming. (sighing) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just... collapse, or something. (shaking head) I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, trying to get everything done, but it's never enough. And then I feel guilty, because I'm not doing enough, or I'm not doing it well enough. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) It's like, I'm just trying to survive, you know? But it's hard to keep going when everything feels so... overwhelming. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I feel like I'm just drowning in all of it, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes... that's been me, too. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and I think it's because of all the emotions swirling around in my head. I'll lie in bed, thinking about everything that's going on, and I just can't seem to turn my brain off. (sighing) I'll worry about the baby, or think about all the things I need to do the next day, or just feel overwhelmed by everything. And even when I do fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious or worried about something. (shaking head) It's like, my mind is just racing all the time, and it's hard to calm it down enough to sleep. (looking down, feeling a bit tearful) Some nights, I'll wake up and just feel so... sad, I guess. Like, I'll be lying there, feeling hopeless, and I won't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just not coming easily to me right now.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump form in throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, like, a deep-down sadness that I just can't shake. (pausing, looking down) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'll be doing something normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making breakfast, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. (sighing) And it's not just about the baby, or being a mom, it's just... everything, I guess. I'll think about my life before the baby, and how I used to be, and I'll just feel so... lost, I guess. (looking up, tearfully) Like, I'm not the same person I used to be, and I don't know how to get back to that. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Some days, it's just hard to get out of bed, because I feel so overwhelmed and sad. And even when I do get up, and I'm taking care of the baby, and doing all the things I'm supposed to do, I still just feel this... emptiness, I guess. (shaking head) It's hard to explain, but it's just this feeling of sadness that's always there, lurking in the background. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) Sometimes I'll just cry, for no reason, because it's just all so... much.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling tears well up in my eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be doing something, and suddenly I'll feel this overwhelming sadness, and I'll just start crying. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's not just when something's wrong, either. Sometimes I'll be happy, or at least, I'll be feeling okay, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. (shaking head) It's like, my emotions are just all over the place, and I don't know how to control them. (looking down, feeling a tear roll down my cheek) I'll cry when I'm feeding the baby, or when I'm changing their diaper, or just when I'm sitting there, holding them. (sighing) It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed by everything, and I don't know how to process it all. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll cry because I'm feeling guilty, or because I'm feeling like I'm not doing enough, or just because I'm feeling so... alone, I guess. (looking up, tearfully) It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm a new mom, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time, but really, I'm just feeling so... sad, and overwhelmed, and alone. (pausing, feeling a sob rise up in my throat) Sorry... (starting to cry)
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(looking down, feeling a mix of emotions) Yes... I have had thoughts like that. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's not like I want to hurt myself, or that I'm planning to do anything, it's just... sometimes the feelings of sadness and overwhelm get so strong, and I don't know how to make them stop. (shaking head) And in those moments, I might think something like, "I don't know if I can do this anymore," or "I feel like I'm such a burden to everyone." (looking up, tearfully) It's like, my mind is just trying to find a way to escape the pain, I guess. (pausing, feeling a sense of shame) But it's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I want to think about. (looking down, feeling a sense of vulnerability) It's just... sometimes, when everything feels too much, my mind goes to some pretty dark places. (pausing, taking a deep breath) But I want you to know that I'm not planning to hurt myself, and I'm not going to act on those thoughts. (looking up, sincerely) I just need help, I guess. I need help finding a way to manage these feelings, and to feel like I can keep going, even when things get tough.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns following the birth of their baby, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure in activities, anxiety, guilt, and difficulty coping with daily responsibilities. They have expressed feelings of being overwhelmed and struggling to adjust to their new role as a mother.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 24, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient indicates laughing doesn't come as easily as it used to and they're trying to be happy but it's not feeling natural, matching 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have definitely looked forward with less enjoyment to things compared to before, as they mention not feeling like doing things they used to enjoy and finding activities dull.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong tendency to self-blame, not only in relation to caring for the baby but also in other aspects of life, such as household chores, and this self-blame occurs frequently, aligning with 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports being anxious or worried all the time, with constant and intrusive thoughts about the baby's safety and well-being, as well as their own ability to care for the baby, indicating a high level of anxiety.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense feelings of panic and fear, even when there is no apparent reason for it, indicating a high level of distress and loss of control.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>Patient reports having a lot of trouble sleeping due to overwhelming emotions, worry, and anxiety, indicating difficulty sleeping most of the time.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports crying frequently, even when feeling happy or okay, and experiences overwhelming sadness, indicating a high level of unhappiness and crying, matching 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of self-harm, but emphasizes they are not planning to act on them and are seeking help to manage their feelings, which aligns with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses suggest a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med> and <med>anxiety</med>, with symptoms including <sym>persistent sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>guilt</sym>, and <sym>difficulty coping with daily responsibilities</sym>. The <med>EPDS</med> score of 24 indicates a probable depression, and the patient's expression of self-harm thoughts is a critical safety concern. According to <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>, the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a depressive episode with peripartum onset. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or a crisis helpline if they experience any thoughts of self-harm
3. Recommend <med>postpartum support groups</med> or online resources for new mothers
4. Suggest <med>mindfulness practices</med> and <med>relaxation techniques</med> to help manage <sym>anxiety</sym> and <sym>stress</sym>
5. Emphasize importance of <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> and self-care activities
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
